entities.name: Stephen of Tournai
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Stephen of Tournai was a Canon regular of Sainte-Geneviève (Paris), and Roman Catholic canonist who became bishop of Tournai in 1192. As a prominent theologian and jurist, he played a key role in the development of canon law and its application in the medieval Church. His most notable work, the 'Liber Extra', is a comprehensive collection of canon law that remains influential to this day.

Stephen's episcopacy was marked by his efforts to reform the Church's administrative structures and promote the use of vernacular languages in liturgical services. His approach to ecclesiastical governance was characterized by a mix of traditionalism and reform, reflecting the complexities of the medieval Church.

Despite his significant contributions to the Church, Stephen's legacy has been somewhat overshadowed by the more prominent figures of his time. Nevertheless, his work on canon law and ecclesiastical governance continues to be studied by scholars today, providing valuable insights into the development of the medieval Church.

The 13th-century historian, Guillaume de Nangis, described Stephen as 'a man of great learning and piety', whose 'excellence in the study of the law' was 'unmatched' among his contemporaries.
